text: When you design a REST API, you should follow some best practices. First, use clear and logical endpoints, such as /users or /products, so developers can easily understand them. Second, always return the correct HTTP status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found. Third, write good documentation that explains how each endpoint works and what data it needs. Finally, use versioning, for example /v1/users, so you can update your API without breaking existing applications. These simple rules make your API easier to use, maintain, and improve over time.
